questions.q: Tuberculosis of bone and joints is also known as:
questions.exp: TB of bone and joints is also known as caries / Koch's disease. (Book p148)

questions.q: Compared with pyogenic bone infections, TB of bone and joints has:
questions.exp: TB of bone and joints has less severe local manifestation compared to pyogenic bacteria. (Book p148)

questions.q: TB of bone is characteristically a:
opts: Paucibacillary infection by Koch's weak bacillus
questions.exp: It is a paucibacillary infection by Koch's weak bacillus (Mycobacterium tuberculosis). (Book p148)

questions.q: The usual route of spread of TB to bone and joints is:
questions.exp: Route: hematogenous (from a primary source). (Book p148)

questions.q: The most common site of TB in the body is the:
questions.exp: Most common site in the body: lung. (Book p148)

questions.q: In the musculoskeletal system, the order of most common sites of TB is:
questions.exp: In musculoskeletal system: spine (TB spondylitis) > hip > knee. (Book p148)

questions.q: In TB of the spine, the regional order of involvement is:
questions.exp: In spine: dorso-lumbar > dorsal > lumbar. (Book p148)

questions.q: In children, the commonest spinal region for TB is the:
questions.exp: In children: cervical spine. (Book p148)

questions.q: Caries sicca refers to:
questions.exp: Variant: caries sicca = TB shoulder. (Book p148)

questions.q: Caries sicca (TB shoulder) is a:
questions.exp: Caries sicca is a dry / non-exudative TB. (Book p148)

questions.q: Spina ventosa is TB of the:
questions.exp: Variant: spina ventosa = TB fingers. (Book p148)

questions.q: The 'filling up of air' like appearance of the fingers on X-ray is the variant known as:
questions.exp: Spina ventosa (TB fingers) shows a 'filling up of air' like appearance. (Book p148)

questions.q: The most common type of TB spine (TB spondylitis / Pott's spine) is:
questions.exp: Types: paradiscal (m/c), central, anterior / wet / exudative (in children), posterior (rarest). (Book p148)

questions.q: The rarest type of TB spine is:
questions.exp: Posterior is the rarest type of TB spine. (Book p148)

questions.q: The 'anterior / wet / exudative' type of TB spine is seen in:
questions.exp: Anterior / wet / exudative type occurs in children. (Book p148)

questions.q: In the central type of TB spine, the primary lesion is in the:
questions.exp: The central type involves the central vertebral body. (Book p148)

questions.q: The paradiscal type of TB spine involves:
opts: The para-vertebral area (bone) and the intervertebral disc
questions.exp: Paradiscal: para-vertebral area (bone) and intervertebral disc are involved. (Book p148)

questions.q: In paradiscal TB spine, how many vertebrae are typically involved?
questions.exp: Paradiscal: 3 vertebrae involved. (Book p149)

questions.q: Paradiscal TB spine characteristically involves:
opts: Upper half of upper vertebra + disc + lower half of lower vertebra
Lower half of upper vertebra + disc + upper half of lower vertebra
questions.exp: Lower half of upper vertebra + disc + upper half of lower vertebra. (Book p149)

questions.q: Three vertebrae are involved in paradiscal TB because they:
opts: Are innervated by a single nerve
Develop from a common somite / sclerotome, giving a common blood supply
Are the largest bones of the spine
questions.exp: d/t development from common somite / sclerotome -> common blood supply. (Book p149)

questions.q: In TB spine, the lesion lies in relation to the spinal cord:
questions.exp: The paradiscal lesion is anterior to the spinal cord. (Book p149)

questions.q: As per the vertebral anatomy diagram, the spinal nerve exits through the:
questions.exp: The spinal nerve exits through the intervertebral foramen. (Book p149)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional feature of TB spine?
questions.exp: Constitutional features: low grade fever, malaise, night pains, evening rise of temperature. (Book p149)

questions.q: The earliest SYMPTOM of TB spine is:
questions.exp: Back pain is the earliest symptom; paraspinal spasm / tenderness is the earliest sign. (Book p149)

questions.q: The earliest SIGN of TB spine is:
questions.exp: Paraspinal spasm / tenderness is the earliest sign. (Book p149)

questions.q: Paraspinal spasm in TB spine produces the characteristic:
questions.exp: Paraspinal spasm / tenderness -> military attitude with cautious gait. (Book p149)

questions.q: The 'knuckle' sign in TB spine is:
questions.exp: Knuckle: prominence of 1 spinous process. (Book p149)

questions.q: 'Gibbus' in TB spine denotes prominence of:
questions.exp: Gibbus: prominence of 2-3 spinous processes. (Book p149)

questions.q: Angular kyphosis in TB spine is defined as prominence of:
questions.exp: Angular kyphosis: prominence of >3 spinous processes. (Book p149)

questions.q: The abscess characteristically seen in TB spine is a:
questions.exp: Cold abscess is a local finding in TB spine. (Book p149)

questions.q: Deformity in TB spine results from:
questions.exp: Deformity d/t vertebral collapse. (Book p149)

questions.q: The earliest X-ray finding in TB spine is:
opts: Disc space narrowing (d/t destruction / dissection of disc)
questions.exp: Disc space narrowing (d/t destruction / dissection of disc): earliest on X-ray. (Book p149)

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT seen on X-ray in TB spine?
questions.exp: X-ray: disc space narrowing, para-vertebral abscess, vertebral lysis. Periosteal reaction is not seen in tubercular osteomyelitis. (Book p149)

questions.q: The investigation of choice (IOC) for TB spine is:
questions.exp: MRI: IOC - shows disc involvement and paradiscal disease involving bone and cartilage. (Book p149)

questions.q: MRI in TB spine demonstrates:
opts: Disc involvement and paradiscal disease involving bone and cartilage
questions.exp: MRI: disc involved + paradiscal disease involving bone and cartilage. (Book p149)

questions.q: The gold standard for diagnosis of TB spine is:
questions.exp: CT guided biopsy: gold standard - organism identified from tissue. (Book p149)

questions.q: Neglected TB spine leads to:
questions.exp: Neglected TB spine -> bony ankylosis. (Book p149)

questions.q: When TB is anywhere else (other sites), the resulting ankylosis is typically:
questions.exp: Note: TB anywhere else -> fibrous ankylosis. (Book p149)

questions.q: Pott's paraplegia results when:
opts: TB hip extends to the cord
TB spine (Pott's spine) compresses the spinal cord, causing neurological manifestations
questions.exp: TB spine (Pott's spine) -> compresses on spinal cord -> neurological manifestations. (Book p150)

questions.q: All of the following are causes of Pott's paraplegia EXCEPT:
opts: Thrombosis of spinal artery with ischaemia
questions.exp: Causes: 1. mechanical (d/t granulation tissue), 2. cord edema (d/t inflammation), 3. thrombosis of spinal artery -> ischaemia. (Book p150)

questions.q: Rapid-onset paraplegia with poor prognosis in Pott's disease is due to:
opts: Thrombosis of the spinal artery causing ischaemia of the spinal cord
questions.exp: Thrombosis of spinal artery -> ischaemia of spinal cord -> rapid onset paraplegia (poor prognosis). (Book p150)

questions.q: The early neurological manifestations of Pott's paraplegia are UMN findings, e.g.:
opts: Ankle clonus, exaggerated deep tendon reflexes, extensor plantar
questions.exp: Early neurological manifestations (UMN findings): ankle clonus / exaggerated deep tendon reflexes, extensor plantar. (Book p150)

questions.q: The LATE feature of Pott's paraplegia that marks a poor prognosis is:
questions.exp: Late: bowel and bladder involvement -> poor prognosis. (Book p150)

questions.q: Which age carries a BETTER prognosis in Pott's paraplegia?
questions.exp: Prognostic factors: younger age -> better prognosis; older -> bad. (Book p150)

questions.q: The speed of onset predicting a BETTER prognosis in Pott's paraplegia is:
questions.exp: Speed of onset: slow -> better prognosis; rapid -> bad. (Book p150)

questions.q: A BETTER prognosis in Pott's paraplegia is associated with an onset that is:
questions.exp: Onset: early -> better prognosis; late -> bad. (Book p150)

questions.q: Duration of cord involvement predicting a BAD prognosis in Pott's paraplegia is:
questions.exp: Duration of cord involvement: shorter history -> better; longer (>1 month) -> bad. (Book p150)
